articles.title: Anthropic appoints Matt Clifford to lead international government affairs
articles.text:
The London-based role will put the former UK AI policy adviser in charge of Anthropic's government engagement outside North America, spanning Europe, Asia-Pacific, and other markets Matt Clifford has joined Anthropic as Managing Director, International Affairs, leading the company's government engagement outside North America Anthropic has appointed Matt Clifford as Managing Director, International Affairs, giving the British technology investor and former UK government AI adviser responsibility for the company's work with governments outside North America. Clifford will be based in London and work across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and other regions. He joins the team led by Mariano-Florentino "Tino" Cuéllar, who recently joined Anthropic and is overseeing its international engagement. The appointment brings someone who has worked on both sides of the technology-policy relationship into a senior role at one of the major AI labs. Clifford co-founded Entrepreneurs First, chairs the UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA), and has advised the UK Government on AI policy and strategy. In 2023, he served as the Prime Minister's Representative for the AI Safety Summit, leading UK preparations and negotiations for the international gathering at Bletchley Park. Cuéllar also credits him with helping design the taskforce that became the UK's AI Safety Institute and authoring the AI Opportunities Action Plan. Clifford said on LinkedIn that his new role would focus on how governments influence the development and use of artificial intelligence. "I've spent the last few years working on some of the big questions that AI poses to governments and countries," he wrote. "It's clear that the decisions that will shape AI's impact shouldn't be made by any one actor - it will take industry, governments and civil society working together." He added: "People everywhere want real agency over how this technology is built and used in their societies, and they should have it. Anthropic takes that seriously, which is why I'm joining." From UK AI policy to a global lab Clifford's move follows several years of increasingly direct involvement in public AI policy. Alongside his work on the 2023 AI Safety Summit, he has continued to chair ARIA, the publicly funded research and development agency. He will remain Chair of both ARIA and Entrepreneurs First while stepping back from his other commitments to focus on Anthropic. Cuéllar said Clifford's combination of technology-building and government experience was central to the appointment. "Few people have both built in this industry and helped shape the public institutions that govern it," Cuéllar wrote on LinkedIn. He added that Clifford would help Anthropic engage with governments "across the globe" as countries make decisions about AI development and adoption. Clifford's move also places him among a growing group of prominent British political and technology figures taking roles with major AI labs. George Osborne has joined OpenAI, while Tom Blomfield and former UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak have joined Anthropic.

articles.text: Edition IN IN US GCC English English हिन्दी मराठी ಕನ್ನಡ தமிழ் বাংলা മലയാളം తెలుగు ગુજરાતી Weather Sign In TOI india Gadgets Now Urban Safety Raksha Bandhan Janmashtami Maharashtra Delhi Karnataka Telangana West Bengal Tamil Nadu Andhra Pradesh Uttar Pradesh Gujarat Rajasthan Punjab Odisha Madhya Pradesh Haryana Tripura Uttarakhand Bihar Kerala Assam Arunachal Pradesh Manipur Chhattisgarh Jammu Kashmir Nagaland Jharkhand Meghalaya Himachal Pradesh Web Stories Digital Arrest Operation Sindoor Cancel Patriarchy Lets D Stress Today's ePaper Live News India News Watch: CCTV captures moment Delhi's Satya Niketan building collapsed, leaving 6 dead Trending Iran War Satya Niketan Building Collapse PM Modi Delhi Building Collapse Deaths Vijay Ujjal Bhuyan Manjit Singh Bedi Supreme Court Swatantra Bhardwaj Shardendu Tiwari Iran War Satya Niketan Building Collapse PM Modi Delhi Building Collapse Deaths Vijay Ujjal Bhuyan Manjit Singh Bedi Supreme Court Swatantra Bhardwaj Shardendu Tiwari Iran War Satya Niketan Building Collapse PM Modi Delhi Building Collapse Deaths Vijay Ujjal Bhuyan Manjit Singh Bedi Supreme Court Swatantra Bhardwaj Shardendu Tiwari Watch: CCTV captures moment Delhi's Satya Niketan building collapsed, leaving 6 dead Edited by: Kanchan Yadav / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Sep 07, 2026, 09:25 IST Comments Share AA + Text Size Small Medium Large The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road NEW DELHI: CCTV footage has captured the moment a multi-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area, killing six people and triggering a major rescue operation. The building, which housed a boys' paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus, collapsed around 1.30 pm on Sunday while repair and construction work was underway. The death toll rose to six after one more person rescued during the night was declared dead. The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped. Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Delhi Disaster Management Authority, have been involved in the operation. "One more person was rescued during the night but was brought dead, taking the toll to six," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said, PTI reported. Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has also been ordered. Officials are continuing efforts to trace people allegedly connected with the incident. To the residents, the collapse felt like a quake. “We felt the ground shake. When we ran outside, we saw that a house had completely collapsed,” said Roshan Pal, a student from Lucknow. “When I came out, a cloud of dust was spreading in all directions. That’s when we realised that the building had collapsed. We started removing one part of a wall soon after. Seven students were under it,” said Rahul Gaur, a resident, TOI reported. 10 patients taken to Trauma Centre According to AIIMS, the JPN Apex Trauma Centre received 10 patients injured in the building collapse. Of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while another patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to injuries. Three patients have been admitted and are undergoing treatment. One of them underwent limb surgery, while another patient with minor injuries was discharged after observation. Investigators are examining whether construction work carried out in the basement may have contributed to the collapse. Initial inquiries suggested that the basement was prone to waterlogging, which may have weakened the structure. Investigators are now examining whether construction work aggravated the situation and contributed to the collapse. The MCD is also looking into the matter. Similar concerns over basement work, water accumulation and the structural condition of the building have emerged in the preliminary probe. Police are likely to examine whether permission had been obtained for the work and why construction was being carried out during the monsoon, sources said. "The building owner, contractor and labourers will be interrogated," an investigator said, TOI reported. It was not immediately clear whether the building owner had obtained permission for the construction or whether the work was being carried out illegally, allegedly in connivance with local authorities. MCD orders demolition of dangerous building According to the MCD, the premises of Building/House No. 13, Satya Niketan, New Delhi, was found to be in a "ruinous, dangerous condition" and posed a threat to people occupying, visiting or passing by the building as well as those in the neighbourhood. Under Section 348 of the DMC Act, 1957, read with Section 491 of the Act, the MCD has ordered the property to be demolished within three days of receipt of the order. The order said that if the owner fails to comply within the specified period, the MCD will demolish the building and recover the demolition charges as arrears of tax. The collapse has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated areas of Delhi. Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations. “What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said. NEW DELHI: A video showing a security official pulling the hair of BRS MLA and former Telangana minister Sabitha Indra Reddy during a protest outside the state assembly in Hyderabad has triggered a political row. The incident took place on Monday as Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) legislators protested against the Congress-led government, alleging that it had failed to fulfil its election promises even after completing 1,000 days in office. Visuals shared by the BRS on X purportedly show security personnel trying to remove Sabitha Indra Reddy from the protest site. During the confrontation, a security official is seen pulling her by her hair as she is taken away from the assembly premises. The BRS alleged that the MLA was dragged away despite being a woman legislator. In its post on X, the BRS said, "Police's inhuman behavior towards former minister and MLA Sabeeta Indra Reddy at the assembly! Police dragging her away brutally by her hair without even considering that she is a woman MLA! Is this the respect the Congress government gives to women?" BRS protests over 1,000 days of Congress rule The incident occurred amid heightened tensions outside the Telangana assembly on the opening day of its monsoon session. BRS legislators and MLCs had arrived wearing black T-shirts carrying slogans targeting the Congress government's performance after 1,000 days in power. The party has accused the ruling government of failing to deliver on its election promises. The ensuing confrontation led to pushing and jostling between BRS members and police. BRS working president KT Rama Rao, former minister T Harish Rao and several other party leaders were detained after being stopped from entering the assembly. They were later shifted away from the protest site. Police, however, said the legislators were stopped because of slogans printed on their black T-shirts and that officers were acting on the instructions of the assembly Speaker. A senior police official said allegations of misconduct would be examined using video footage. The BRS has condemned the action and said it would raise the issue with the assembly Speaker. articles.text: Torrential rain causes widespread damage; while north-west South Africa hit by thunderstorms and central-southern US faces oppressive heat  Typhoon Saudel brought days of torrential rain to the Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces in south-east China last week. The city of Putian, in Fujian province, recorded 416.5mm of rain in a 24-hour period between Thursday and Friday, with surrounding villages recording more than 500mm in the same period. In Fujian, authorities estimate that almost 600,000 people were evacuated from high-risk, flood-prone areas. A further 128,000 people in 53 counties were also affected across Jiangxi, with emergency evacuations affecting 9,000 people.  Flooding, landslips and infrastructure damage were reported widely in the region. More than 2,500 teachers and students were trapped in a school compound in the Zhejiang city of Wenzhou on Wednesday after extreme rainfall caused flash floods in low-lying areas. At least 1,260 people reportedly had to be rescued in Putian after a river embankment collapsed on Thursday, flattening 100 homes. On Saturday, a landslip in a village of Suichuan county, in Jiangxi province, killed three people and nine others remaining missing.   Continue reading...

The probe further intensified with the owner of the building being apprehended in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan, following a massive multi-state manhunt involving 10 police teams. Delhi Police had earlier issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against him after he went untraceable following the collapse. The suspended officials include the MCD Deputy Commissioner, Executive Engineer, Superintending Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Junior Engineer. The action came as authorities faced questions over the safety of the decades-old building, which was being used as a boys' paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus. The multi-storey building collapsed at around 1.30 pm on Sunday while repair work was underway. Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Delhi Disaster Management Authority, continued rescue operations through the night. Death toll rises as rescue continues So far, 12 people have been pulled out of the debris, with seven reported dead earlier in the rescue operation. The search continued on Monday as teams worked through the remaining debris to determine whether anyone else was trapped. National Disaster Response Force Inspector General (IG) Narendra Bundela said the force did not have a "specific figure" on the number of people trapped under the debris. According to Bundela, the rescue operation involving the NDRF and agencies of the Delhi government was expected to continue until late Monday. The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) said 11 patients had been received at the JPN Apex Trauma Centre following the collapse. "Out of the 11 patients, five were brought dead, while one patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to his injuries; three patients have been admitted and are being treated. One patient underwent limb surgery. One patient had sustained a minor injury and was discharged after observation," the statement read. Water, repair work under scanner Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta visited Satya Niketan on Monday to review the rescue operation. She said around 80% of the debris had been cleared, with teams focusing on the basement. Gupta said water accumulation in the basement, combined with repair work on the old structure, led to the collapse. "Approximately 80 per cent of the debris has been cleared, with only the basement debris remaining. Water had accumulated in the basement, and the combination of this with ongoing repair work on the old structure led to the collapse," she said. The chief minister ordered the sealing of buildings in Delhi having a fifth floor and warned of action against officials found responsible. "Strict action will be taken against MCD officials found responsible. Instructions have been issued to immediately seal buildings in Delhi having a fifth floor," she said in a statement. Gupta also said the building adjacent to the collapsed structure would be demolished after the debris was cleared, as it was considered extremely dangerous. "Residents of the collapsed building and adjacent unsafe buildings have been evacuated. The standing building, which appears extremely dangerous, will be demolished once the debris is cleared," Gupta said. City-wide safety checks ordered The Delhi government has ordered structural audits of similar buildings, with a policy being drafted to make owners of old buildings submit safety reports before operating PG accommodations, nursing homes, schools or other commercial establishments. Officials found responsible for negligence will also face immediate action," she said. The government had earlier ordered a magisterial inquiry and an FIR against the building owner following an on-site review. "Following an on-site review and based on the preliminary assessment, the chief minister has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident and FIR against the building owner," the Delhi CMO had said in a post on X. Residents said many students staying in the area were from Keralam, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh and studied at nearby colleges including Motilal Nehru College, Atma Ram Sanatan Dharm College and Sri Venkateswara College. The building, which housed a boys' paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus, collapsed around 1.30 pm on Sunday while repair and construction work was underway. The death toll rose to six after one more person rescued during the night was declared dead. The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped. Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Delhi Disaster Management Authority, have been involved in the operation. "One more person was rescued during the night but was brought dead, taking the toll to six," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said, PTI reported. Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has also been ordered. Officials are continuing efforts to trace people allegedly connected with the incident. To the residents, the collapse felt like a quake. “We felt the ground shake. When we ran outside, we saw that a house had completely collapsed,” said Roshan Pal, a student from Lucknow. “When I came out, a cloud of dust was spreading in all directions. That’s when we realised that the building had collapsed. We started removing one part of a wall soon after. Seven students were under it,” said Rahul Gaur, a resident, TOI reported. 10 patients taken to Trauma Centre According to AIIMS, the JPN Apex Trauma Centre received 10 patients injured in the building collapse. Of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while another patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to injuries. Three patients have been admitted and are undergoing treatment. One of them underwent limb surgery, while another patient with minor injuries was discharged after observation. Investigators are examining whether construction work carried out in the basement may have contributed to the collapse. Initial inquiries suggested that the basement was prone to waterlogging, which may have weakened the structure. Investigators are now examining whether construction work aggravated the situation and contributed to the collapse. The MCD is also looking into the matter. Similar concerns over basement work, water accumulation and the structural condition of the building have emerged in the preliminary probe. Police are likely to examine whether permission had been obtained for the work and why construction was being carried out during the monsoon, sources said. "The building owner, contractor and labourers will be interrogated," an investigator said, TOI reported. It was not immediately clear whether the building owner had obtained permission for the construction or whether the work was being carried out illegally, allegedly in connivance with local authorities. MCD orders demolition of dangerous building According to the MCD, the premises of Building/House No. 13, Satya Niketan, New Delhi, was found to be in a "ruinous, dangerous condition" and posed a threat to people occupying, visiting or passing by the building as well as those in the neighbourhood. Under Section 348 of the DMC Act, 1957, read with Section 491 of the Act, the MCD has ordered the property to be demolished within three days of receipt of the order. The order said that if the owner fails to comply within the specified period, the MCD will demolish the building and recover the demolition charges as arrears of tax. The collapse has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated areas of Delhi. Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations. “What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said. articles.text: Populist, far-right, anti-immigration AfD wins vote in eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. Plus, 50 years since The Muppet Show first hit our screens      Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here      Good morning. A far-right leader who has won an important state election in Germany has  thanked Elon Musk for his support , as voices in Europe warn the result is a serious moment for the continent. No far-right party has led or formed a government in Germany since the defeat of nazism at the end of the second world war.  Ulrich Siegmund, the Alternative für Deutschland’s lead candidate, thanked Musk on X after the tech billionaire said “Well done!” in German to the AfD co-founder Alice Weidel. The populist, far-right, anti-immigration party won the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.   Will the AfD be able to form a state government?  Despite its resounding victory, the party fell just short of a majority. It was seeking an absolute majority in the state legislature to govern alone and overcome the so-called “firewall” of the mainstream parties, which refuse to work with it. The final results showed the AfD falling three seats short, with 39 lawmakers in an 83-member legislature.   What has been the reaction in Washington and Moscow?  Donald Trump posted a screenshot of the election projection without comment on his Truth Social site. The Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev took a screengrab of Trump’s post and praised a “historic win for the pragmatic AfD”. The AfD is pro-Kremlin, urging a stop to support for Ukraine and pushing for Ukrainians in Germany to no longer receive refugee status.   Who else has been saying Trump’s war may not achieve its aims?  The US energy secretary, Chris Wright, said on Sunday morning  Washington might not be able to reach an agreement with Tehran  that would prevent Iran from having nuclear weapons. “We are strangling their economy to try to bring either a change in policy from the existing regime or a new regime,” he said. Hours after the building collapse in a student-dominated area near Delhi University’s South Campus, the MCD has ordered action against illegal buildings with four or more storeys. One more body was recovered during late-night operations, taking the total number of fatalities to six. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police and other agencies continued rescue operations at the site as they worked to remove the debris. The collapse that took place on Sunday afternoon, has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest (PG) accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated parts of the national capital. The Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident and directed that an FIR be registered against the building owner, the chief minister’s office (CMO) said. The decision was taken following an on-site review and a preliminary assessment of the incident, the CMO said. “Following an on-site review and based on the preliminary assessment, the chief minister has ordered a Magisterial Inquiry of the incident and an FIR against the building owner,” the CMO said. It added that those found responsible for the incident would be held fully accountable and face the strictest provisions of the law. Meanwhile, Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations. She said students are sent to Delhi with hopes of building their future and questioned who would be held responsible for their safety. “What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said. Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed as an isolated case, claiming that similar incidents occur every few months. He also raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of Delhi. Saigal alleged that some buildings either have unapproved blueprints, additional floors added later or substandard construction, and questioned whether authorities responsible for approving building plans had adequately checked their safety. "Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi - I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said. He also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded and over-built, saying authorities should consider stopping the sanctioning of new building plans in such areas and examine the safety of existing structures. "At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new construction—or stop sanctioning building plans—for areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added. NSUI President Vinod Jakhar described the situation as extremely grave and said rescue operations were continuing under difficult conditions. "Rescue operations are ongoing, and conditions are dire. Almost all the students being pulled out are dead. We tried our best to get those students out; we actually succeeded in rescuing about three of them. Had the medical facilities, medical teams, police, and fire brigade arrived on time—had all necessary resources and responsible officials been present promptly—perhaps more students could have been saved. But the BJP has no disaster management plan. Just look at how the country's Home Minister inaugurates a grand BJP office in Goa today, while here, a building collapses. BJP offices never collapse because they are built using money extorted from PG and coaching centre operators. Our only demand is justice for the students. Several of our colleagues have also sustained serious injuries. There is absolutely no accountability," Jakhar told news agency ANI. Meanwhile, Delhi Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha president Rajat Choudhary said the situation remained serious and appealed for speedy rescue efforts. He said ambulances and doctors were present in large numbers and urged both the Delhi and Central governments to ensure that those trapped were rescued quickly. Choudhary also appealed to political parties to avoid politicising the tragedy and instead extend support to the affected families and those involved in the rescue operation.
